summary.headline: Gulshan Polyols Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 121% YoY to INR 65 crore on 11.9% margin, driven by ethanol; FY26 PAT INR 107 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 550 crore (up 7% YoY) and EBITDA INR 65 crore (up 121%), with margin up 612 bps to 11.9%. Ethanol drove the improvement on higher utilisation and softer maize and rice input costs, while grain processing stayed weak at a 2.1% margin. Q4 PAT was INR 38 crore (up 435%) and FY26 PAT INR 107 crore (up 334%). Management said the ethanol order book fell to 18 crore litres from 21 crore litres last year, below the 23 crore litres it had applied for, and it expects top-ups in the next tenders.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,609 crore, EBITDA INR 201 crore, margin 12.5%; management says it is over 60% of revenue and profit. Installed capacity about 810 KLPD.

segments.name: Grain processing (sorbitol, starch, fructose)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 610 crore, EBITDA INR 13 crore, margin 2.1%, held back by pricing. Management targets about 5% EBITDA margin (about INR 40 crore) on INR 800 crore revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 93 crore, EBITDA INR 23 crore, margin 24.2%; described as a steady cash-flow contributor.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR 2,600-2,800 crore: ethanol INR 1,800-1,900 crore, grain INR 800 crore, mineral INR 100 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 10-12% and PAT margin at 5-6%.
Utilisation target of 80-90% across key divisions; up to INR 3,000 crore revenue possible at 100% utilisation with the current setup.
Ethanol order book to rise from 18 crore litres to at least 22 crore litres within FY27, via tenders expected in June (C2 and C3 cycles).
Management expects to sustain current ethanol margins for the next two to three years while FCI rice remains available.

Debt-free by FY29 except the Assam plant long-term loan, which runs to FY32. PLI: MP for seven years, Assam for three years; total PLI about INR 30 crore per annum; INR 5 crore capital subsidy expected in Q1 FY27.

Capex of about INR 500 crore on a 100-acre Narsinghpur (MP) site, to start in FY28 and spread over two to three years; target EBITDA margin of about 15% and ROCE of about 22%. Long-term vision of INR 5,000 crore revenue within about four years.
capex_capacity: Ethanol installed capacity about 810 KLPD; licensed capacity of 26 crore litres per annum against an 18 crore litre order book, leaving headroom to scale up to full utilisation under an E30 mandate.

New capex (about INR 500 crore, specialty and import-substitute chemicals, mostly grain-processing based) to start in FY28; funding is a mix of debt, equity and possible fundraising; Board approval pending.
Possible capacity enhancement of sorbitol and fructose; no ethanol capex planned yet, though capacity may be enhanced over time.
Maize pricing about INR 19-20/kg in the north during Rabi season; the company keeps about 20 days of inventory.
demand_pricing: Ethanol order book of 18 crore litres (about INR 1,250 crore revenue) for ESY 2025-26; the company had applied for 23 crore litres and received 18 crore, against 21 crore litres last year. About 50% already fulfilled by March; about 9 crore litres expected over the remaining two quarters.
Long-term OMC off-take of about 13 crore litres per year through 2032.
Realisations: DDGS INR 21-22/kg (maize) and INR 25-27/kg (rice), adding about INR 10/litre to ethanol economics. Ethanol EBITDA about INR 10-11/litre on a 12% margin.
Sorbitol exported to over 45 countries; export exposure is small at about INR 100 crore. Management says 80-90% of suppliers are domestic.

Maize outlook: INR 19-20/kg in the north now, INR 22 in MP; in H2 FY27 MP may fall to INR 18-19 and Assam/Muzaffarnagar may be around INR 22. Positive EBITDA break-even for ethanol at maize about INR 24/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and how will it be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol order book is 18 crore litres (about INR 1,250 crore), expected to rise to at least 22 crore litres in FY27 through C2 and C3 tenders due in June.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the company for E30 blending and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity of 26 crore litres gives 8 crore litres of unused headroom; management is ready to run at up to 100% once the mandate is given. Government is considering E25, E27 and E30. Management expects FCI rice supply to hold for two to three years, keeping margins steady.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 ethanol volume decline versus the previous year and quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: The ESY 2025-26 allocation fell to 18 crore litres from 21 crore litres, and about 50% was fulfilled by March. Additional allocations are expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is any subsidy included in Q4 results?
qa_highlights.answer: No subsidy was received in Q4; the result is operating profit only. A INR 5 crore capital subsidy for Assam is expected in Q1 FY27, and PLIs are expected by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for grain processing in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the worst is over and targets about 5% EBITDA margin on about INR 800 crore revenue (about INR 40 crore EBITDA) in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: A mega project of about INR 500 crore on the Narsinghpur land, with capex in FY28-29 funded by debt and equity. Target EBITDA margin is about 15% and ROCE about 22%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory build up in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sugar-based ethanol is available only until about March-April, so OMCs lift more from sugar in Q4 and inventory builds. This is a recurring seasonal pattern that has evened out in the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-current investments higher (INR 47 crore versus INR 16 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds were invested in mutual funds to meet bank commitments on minimum working capital utilisation levels.

risks_watch: Ethanol volumes depend on tender allocations; the company received 18 crore litres against 23 crore litres applied for, and the gap must be closed in the June tenders.
Dependence on FCI rice availability (about 40% of feedstock); a change in government supply would affect the cost advantage.
Maize and rice prices, DDGS realisations and seasonal Kharif pricing (INR 18-22/kg) affect ethanol economics.
Grain processing margin remains at 2.1% and depends on import costs and China competition.
Capex funding for the INR 500 crore project is undecided; equity fundraising is possible.
Working capital build-up in Q4 (ethanol inventory) and the company's stated aim of reducing working capital intensity.
Mutual fund investments of INR 47 crore were made to meet bank minimum-utilisation commitments.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on ethanol demand, blending policy and margin sustainability. Evasive on the exact order-book shortfall and on capex funding and timing, which are still under evaluation. Several growth targets are stated without a supporting bridge.
key_quotes: Our ethanol business is now the primary driver of the company, contributing over 60% of both revenue and profitability.
So, definitely, I feel the worst is over for the grain processing division.
So, I don't ever see that demand will be more than supply.
Current order book is definitely lower than what we had applied for and expected.

adds.what: Specialty and import-substitute chemicals capex (about INR 500 crore, Narsinghpur MP 100-acre site)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR 2,600-2,800 crore (about 12-21% over FY26's INR 2,314 crore, midpoint ~17%), backed partly by an ethanol order book of 18 crore litres (targeted to rise to at least 22 crore litres) and existing unused licensed capacity, but the INR 500 crore Narsinghpur capex only starts in FY28 and the ethanol order book is below the 23 crore litres applied for.
